countertops.sourceClass: original research author dissertation abstract at Syracuse repository
countertops.title: Glenn Tristan Thompson, Geochemical and Thermobarometric Constraints on Granite Crystallization
countertops.captureMethod: curl -fL original HTML; root read complete abstract
countertops.passage: Granite is ubiquitously recognized by many people due to its common use as a building material and its abundance in the Earth's continental crust. From countertops to library steps, and as a source of economically important elements, granitic rocks are deeply intertwined with human development.

classification-visual.title: Stephen Earle, Physical Geology
classification-visual.captureMethod: curl -fL original PDF; pypdf page extraction read by /root
classification-visual.passage: VISUAL OBSERVATION by /root: PDF page71 figure3.16 places Granite in felsic/intrusive row with quartz and K/plagioclase feldspar, and Basalt in mafic/extrusive row with ferromagnesian mineral fraction50–100%. The surrounding actual text states ferromagnesian minerals are clearly darker. This supports light granitic versus dark basaltic classification together with text texture definitions.
